concept.title: ArrayStack 的按位插入
concept.core_question: ArrayStack 在位置 i 插入元素时为什么要向右搬移元素？
concept.summary: 插入前需确保容量足够，再把区间 i 到 n-1 右移一格，空出 a[i] 后写入新元素。
concept.definition: ArrayStack 的 add(i,x) 在后备数组已满时先扩容，然后把原有下标 i 至 n-1 的元素按从右到左的安全顺序整体右移一位，把 x 写入 a[i]，最后令 n 增加 1。忽略扩容时，其时间为 $O(n-i)$。

relations.description: 理解《ArrayStack 的按位插入》是继续学习目标知识点的直接基础。

rookie_explanation.analogy: 在坐满一排人的第 i 个位置加入新人时，右侧所有人先各向右挪一位，才能给新人空出连续的位置。
rookie_explanation.boundary: 类比不说明实际实现可能使用批量内存移动，也不包含扩容所需的额外复制成本。

related_concepts.title: 元素数量与数组容量
related_concepts.core_question: 数组式线性表中的元素数量与后备数组容量有什么区别？
related_concepts.summary: 元素数量 n 只统计有效元素，容量 length(a) 是可用槽位总数，必须始终满足 n 不超过容量。
related_concepts.definition: 在数组式线性表中，元素数量 n 表示当前有效元素个数，后备数组容量 length(a) 表示已分配槽位总数。有效元素只占其中一部分，基本不变量是 $0\le n\le \mathrm{length}(a)$；空闲槽位不是逻辑元素。

related_concepts.title: ArrayStack 的操作复杂度
related_concepts.core_question: ArrayStack 各项操作的时间复杂度是什么？
related_concepts.summary: get/set 为 O(1)，add/remove(i) 为 O(1+n-i)，尾端 push/pop 的摊还时间为 O(1)。
related_concepts.definition: ArrayStack 实现 List 接口时，get(i) 与 set(i,x) 的最坏时间为 $O(1)$；忽略 resize，add(i,x) 与 remove(i) 为 $O(1+n-i)$。从空结构开始的更新序列中，resize 总成本为线性，因此在尾端实现 push 与 pop 时每次操作具有 $O(1)$ 摊还时间。

source_records.content: The operations of adding and removing elements from an ArrayStack are illustrated in \figref{arraystack}. To implement the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operation, we first check if \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}} is already full. If so, we call the method \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} to increase the size of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}}. How \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} is implemented will be discussed later. For now, it is sufficient to know that, after a call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}}, we can be sure that $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{length}(\ensuremath{\mathit{a}})}} > \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}$. With this out of the way, we now shift the elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}-1]}}$ right by one position to make room for \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{x}}}}, set \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}]}} equal to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{x}}}}, and increment \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}.

A sequence of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operations on an ArrayStack. Arrows denote elements being copied. Operations that result in a call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} are marked with an asterisk.

If we ignore the cost of the potential call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}}, then the cost of the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operation is proportional to the number of elements we have to shift to make room for \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{x}}}}. Therefore the cost of this operation (ignoring the cost of resizing \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}}) is $O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}})$. Implementing the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operation is similar. We shift the elements $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}+1]}},\ldots,\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}-1]}}$ left by one position (overwriting \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}[\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}]}}) and decrease the value of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}. After doing this, we check if \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}} is getting much smaller than \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{length}(\ensuremath{\mathit{a}})}} by checking if $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{length}(\ensuremath{\mathit{a}})}} \ge 3\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}$. If so, then we call \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{resize}()}} to reduce the size of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{a}}}}.
